value.title: Middleware scope and pipeline order in the dispatcher

acceptanceCriteria.text: With global middleware `g1`, `g2`, prefix middleware `p1` on `/api` registered before `g2` and `p2` on `/api`, and `app.route("/api/users").use(r1).use(r2).get(h)`, a `GET /api/users` records `g1, g2, p1, p2, r1, r2, h`, and `app.get("/b", r3, h2)` makes `GET /b` record `g1, g2, r3, h2`. [D-120; D-119; T35] Decision: all global middleware run first in registration order, then all matching prefix middleware in registration order, however the two kinds of registration interleave. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-1] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

Prefix `/api` runs for `/api` and `/api/users` and not for `/apix` or `/ap`; prefix `/api/` behaves as `/api`, and prefix `/` runs for every path. [D-118; T35] Decision: a trailing `/` of a prefix is ignored and `/` covers every path. User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

With `RouterPolicy.builder().caseInsensitive(true)` the `/api` prefix middleware runs for `/API/users`, and with `mergeSlashes(true)` it runs for `//api//users`, so every path that reaches a route under the prefix runs the prefix middleware. [D-118] Decision: the prefix comparison uses the same case and slash normalisation that the router applies under the app's `RouterPolicy`. User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

Inside prefix middleware and the handler, `req.path()` still returns the full decoded path (for example `/api/users`, not `/users`). [D-118; D-137] Decision: NaruServe does not strip the mount prefix from `req.path()` and has no `baseUrl`. User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

A request that matches no route runs global and matching prefix middleware and then receives the `404` of the fallback point; route middleware of other routes does not run. [D-121; D-117] Decision: for a lookup result other than `MATCHED` the dispatcher builds the `Request` with the parsed `Method` and empty params and runs the global and matching prefix middleware with an empty route middleware list and the fallback answer as the terminal step. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-6] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

A recording global middleware runs once each for a `405` (method mismatch), a `426` (WebSocket-only route without upgrade), an automatic `OPTIONS /r` `204`, a `501` for `TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and a `501` for `CONNECT /`, before the automatic response is written. [D-117; wave decision: Pre-request rejections] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

A global middleware does not run for the pre-request rejections (unrecognised method token `501`, raw path not starting with `/` `400`, `PathValidator` rejection `400`, `OPTIONS *` `204`) nor for the lifecycle-gate `503`s of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.
For a matched route all middleware and the handler run on the adapter thread that called the dispatcher, one after the other. [D-128]

value.requirement: The system shall execute global and matching segment-boundary prefix middleware in their combined registration order, followed by matched route middleware and its handler, or the automatic/static fallback. All continuations remain synchronous and single-use.
value.rationale: Covers D-117, D-118, D-120, D-121 and the wave decision on pre-request rejections (middleware runs for `404`, `405`, `426`, the automatic `OPTIONS` reply and the `501` of a disabled `TRACE` or `CONNECT`, including `CONNECT /`; the static-file and WebSocket-upgrade cases are asserted in waves 6 and 7). T35.
